correctness.rationale: The mixed uniform-circle plus two antipodal atoms measure has exact Gram diag(1,(1+w)/2,(1−w)/2) for 1,cos,sin when 0<w<1; thus its evaluation kernel K_w=1+a cosθ cosφ+b sinθ sinφ with a=2/(1+w), b=2/(1−w). The L∞ projection norm is the maximal L1 kernel-row mass, equal to J_w(t)=(1−w)I(sqrt(b²−(b²−a²)t²))+w·max(1,at) for t=|cosθ|. The formula I(R)=2/π(sqrt(R²−1)+arcsin(1/R)) is obtained by splitting the two sign arcs. On t≤(1+w)/2 the atomic contribution is constant and the continuous term strictly decreases. On the remaining interval the derivative sign reduces to tf(R²)>π(1−w)(1+w)/16, f(s)=sqrt(s−1)/s; its minimum on the interval occurs at an endpoint, whose exact lower bounds follow from 2sqrt(3)>π. Therefore only perpendicular θ=π/2,3π/2 maximize. Row-kernel sign functions characterize norming inputs a.e.; differentiation of the resulting formula proves strict monotonicity, convexity and one-sided limits, excluding w=1. Independent angular row checks at five positive weights and exact mixed moment checks support, not replace, the analytic argument.

value.rationale: The Lebesgue constant is a natural stability measure of real trigonometric least-squares projection. Adding two singular antipodal sample masses introduces a genuine angular optimization problem, resolved for the full weight continuum with unique worst evaluation directions, extremizing inputs, monotonic convex norm profile and singular w→1 boundary. This is an informative stable/unstable mixed-measure exact classification, not a routine kernel-update restatement.

limitations: Only real first-harmonic span with equal antipodal atoms and 0<w<1; w=1 has rank collapse, higher degree and unequal atoms open.
